subject: Onshore data wipe schedule and DPA clause clarifications
messages:
From: Jack Miller <jack.miller@arborhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on onshore wipe timing & purge SLA (DPA redlines attached)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our legal and security teams reviewed the DPA and flagged a few items we'd like to clarify before we circulate redlines back to procurement: 

1) Onshore processing / residency: the DPA states processing will occur in the US unless otherwise agreed. Can you confirm whether any backups, DR replicas, or telemetry dumps may be stored outside the US for short periods for operational reasons? If so, what are the controls, and can we get explicit language limiting any cross-border copies?

2) Deletion and purge SLAs: we need a clear operational SLA for deletions triggered by customer requests (including deletion from backups). We understand active data can be removed quickly, but what is the typical window for backups and immutable snapshots to be purged? Is there an attestation/certificate-of-deletion option?

3) Retention carve-outs: our compliance team asks for explicit carve-outs for (a) anonymized analytics, and (b) lawful hold for litigation. How do you handle these exceptions in practice?

4) Evidence: can you provide a short export of the retention controls and any sample deletion log entries we could attach to our audit package?

Attached: Arbor_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf (redline highlights).

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Wednesday to align?

Thanks,
Jack
Head of Security Operations
Arbor Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jack Miller <jack.miller@arborhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on onshore wipe timing & purge SLA (DPA redlines attached)

Jack —

Really appreciate the detailed read. I've pulled in Lauren (Customer Solutions) and Vivek (Security) to make sure we cover operational and control-level answers. Quick answers below, and then proposed contract language where helpful. Happy to jump on Wed — I have 10:00–11:30 PT open.

1) Backups/DR replicas: Our default is US-only for customer data for the Arbor account. In rare operational situations (e.g., urgent failover testing), ephemeral copies may be created in a nearby region; those are short-lived (<48 hours) and encrypted in-transit and at-rest. We can add explicit text: "No backups, replicas, or telemetry originating from Customer data will be stored outside the United States except for transient operational failover events not exceeding 48 hours, and only if encrypted and logged."

2) Deletion/purge SLA: Operationally, active data deletions are processed within 24–48 hours. Backup/snapshot deletion can take longer depending on retention windows and the backup lifecycle. We propose contract language that reflects our operational model and an optional certificate-of-deletion for enterprise customers: 

Proposed clause (suggestion):
"Upon Customer's verified deletion request, Redwood Inference will: (a) delete Customer Data from active production stores within forty-eight (48) hours; (b) initiate deletion of backups and snapshots and complete deletion within ninety (90) days, except to the extent retention is required by law or subject to an active legal hold; and (c) upon Customer request, provide a certificate of deletion describing the scope and timing of deletion activities."

3) Retention carve-outs: For analytics we can commit to only storing fully pseudonymized aggregates not tied to Customer identifiers and provide examples. Lawful holds are handled per written notice with preservation until the hold is lifted.

4) Evidence: I've attached a short export of our retention policy and sample deletion log entries in the follow-up (Vivek will provide sanitized logs).

Next steps: if the proposed clause above is acceptable as a starting point, we can hand it to Legal to produce a redline for your counsel. If you'd like the deletion certificate as a line item in the contract, we can add that to the SOW / enterprise addendum (may affect lead time).

Call availability: Wed 10:30 PT works for me — can you confirm?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jack Miller <jack.miller@arborhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@arborhealth.com
Date: 2026-09-22T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on onshore wipe timing & purge SLA (DPA redlines attached)

Soojin — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups before we bring this to counsel:

- 90 days for backups is reasonable, but our security team prefers a shorter certified window for customer-initiated erasures if possible. Is there any way to commit to a 60-day certified window for enterprise customers on a paid add-on?

- For the transient cross-border copies: can you confirm there is no secondary copy retained beyond the 48 hours and that we would receive an audit log entry when those events occur?

- Certificate of deletion: we'll want a templated format that includes a checksum or identifier for the dataset removed, a timestamp, and an operator signature (or signed assertion from Redwood). Is that something you can supply?

Attaching Arbor security questionnaire for your security team's review — we highlighted the relevant retention/wipe rows.

On the call: 10:30 PT on Wed works for me.

Thanks,
Jack

Jack / team —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and formal next steps so procurement/ legal have something to work from: 

1) Wording we will propose in the DPA (legal will produce redline):
"Redwood Inference shall not store Customer Data outside the United States except for transient operational failover events not to exceed forty-eight (48) hours in any single event, which events will be logged and encrypted. Redwood will provide Customer with audit log entries for any such events upon request."

2) Deletion / backup SLA options:
- Standard (no charge): Active data deleted within 48 hours; backups initiated for deletion and completed within 90 days.
- Enterprise add-on (paid): Active data deleted within 24 hours; accelerated backup purge completed within 60 days plus a signed certificate-of-deletion in standardized format (includes dataset id, timestamp, and Redwood operator assertion).

3) Retention carve-outs & lawful hold: Lawful and regulatory holds will be honored upon written notice; anonymized analytics will be kept only as pseudonymized aggregates and explicitly excluded from the definition of "Customer Personal Data".

4) Evidence package: Vivek will share a sanitized sample deletion log and a one-page controls export (attached). Expect those artifacts to arrive within 48 hours.

Action items:
- Redwood Legal to ship formal redline for the DPA by 2026-09-25 (Soojin / Lauren).
- Arbor to review and confirm whether you want the Enterprise add-on with the 60-day certificate option (Jack / legal).
- I will upload the redline and artifacts to the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4892

Attached: DPA_redline_suggestion.docx (proposed language + optional addendum).

If you want the certificate format now, I'll paste a template into the redline doc. Otherwise, we can include it as an SOW attachment.

Appreciate the collaboration — we want this to be predictable for your auditors.
